mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6% for two consecutive months indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the following 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS YoY growth falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening coupled with rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their 4-quarter moving averages indicates a broad-based decline in economic activity and housing demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both below 4-quarter moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both GDP and housing are below their 4-quarter averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during four-month stretches of above-average payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between rising real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting rapid demand transmission to equity valuations in the short run.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises month-over-month.
